'''Paul Anthony'''<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 6, 2023 |title=Paul Anthony Wender |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/paul-anthony-wender |access-date=December 19, 2023 |website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences |language=en}}</ref> '''Wender''' is an American chemist whose work is focused on [[organic chemistry]], [[organometallic chemistry]], synthesis, [[catalysis]], [[chemical biology]], imaging, drug delivery, and molecular therapeutics. He is currently the [[Francis William Bergstrom|Francis W. Bergstrom]] Professor of Chemistry at [[Stanford University]] and is an elected fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellow/wender-paul |title=Paul Wender |publisher=aaas.org |accessdate=May 12, 2017 }}{{Dead link|date=May 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/paul-wender |title=Paul Wender |publisher=stanford.edu |accessdate=May 12, 2017}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Born in 1947,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Department of Chemistry |first=Stanford University |date=Jul 3, 2017 |title=On Saturday, the Wender Symposium celebrated Professor Paul Wender's 70th Birthday and 45 years of world-class science from the Wender Lab! |url=https://twitter.com/stanforduchem/status/881910607884292099 |access-date=July 18, 2017 |website=[[Twitter]] |language=en}}</ref> Wender received a B.S. from [[Wilkes University]] in 1969, and a Ph.D. degree from [[Yale University]] in 1973.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paul Wender's Profile {{!}} Stanford Profiles |url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/paul-wender |access-date=July 28, 2020 |website=profiles.stanford.edu |language=en}}</ref> At Yale he worked with Frederick E. Ziegler, graduating with a thesis on the transformation of ketones into nitriles, and the [[total synthesis]] of [[Eremophila neglecta|eremophilone]]. He was a post-doctoral fellow at Columbia University in 1974. In 1974, he began his independent career as an assistant professor and later associate professor at [[Harvard University]]. In 1982, he became a professor at Stanford University. He is currently the Francis W. Bergstrom Professor of Chemistry there.

His research involves the targeted synthesis of complex biologically interesting molecules. He  coined the term "function-oriented synthesis." He pursues applications for drugs in cancer therapy, for example, and synthesized [[phorbol]], [[Paclitaxel|taxol]], [[resiniferatoxin]] and prostatin, among others. Because of his work on the synthesis of indole derivatives, the Wender indole synthesis he described in 1981 was named after him.
